summary: Albany County lookout: a wooden platform in 1911, a 60-foot steel tower with an observatory in 1927, removed in the 1960s; no remains described.

facts.design: Wooden platform (1911), then a glassed-in observatory atop a 60-foot steel tower (1927)
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com list the tower as gone; no source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Wooden platform placed at the site (register). A May 1911 newspaper item describes a phone line and a lookout station to be kept.
Man assigned as the lookout resigned, unable to climb the tower ladder; the post was not filled
New steel tower with a glassed-in observatory replaced the wooden platform
Oscar Shoemaker served as lookout (register and firelookout.com)
Register says removed in the 1960s; 1960 is approximate

evidence.supports: first lookout location 1911: a wooden platform
evidence.quote: The site first became a lookout location in 1911 when a wooden platform was placed at the site.

evidence.supports: 1927 new steel tower replaced the earlier structure
evidence.quote: This structure served until 1927 when a new steel tower was erected.
Oscar Shoemaker served as the lookout at the site in 1932.

evidence.supports: 1930 Casper paper: primary lookouts on Somber Hill and Medicine Bow Peak, manned June to October
evidence.quote: primary lookouts on Somber Hill and Medicine Bow Peak, which are manned continually between June and October.
Gone. Known lookout personnel: 1932: Oscar Shoemaker.

evidence.supports: May 1911 phone line between Foxpark and Somber hill, lookout station to be maintained
evidence.quote: The forest service is building a phone line between Foxpark and Somber hill, where a lookout station will be maintained.

evidence.supports: 1927 observatory at the top of a 60-foot steel tower
evidence.quote: The observatory is a glassed-in house at the top of a 60-foot steel tower.

evidence.supports: 1922 Lee Hall resigned, dizziness and the ladder
evidence.quote: has been compelled to resign, being unable, on account of dizziness, to ascend the ladder on the tower.
The place has not been filled.

evidence.supports: July 1922: Somber Hill called a secondary lookout
evidence.quote: Somber Hill is a secondary lookout

evidence.supports: primary lookout on Medicine Bow peak
evidence.quote: remains all the time on the primary lookout

evidence.supports: September 1922 smoke reported from Somber Hill tower
evidence.quote: Forest Guard Benham reported smoke from Somber Hill lookout tower today

evidence.supports: cross bearing from Medicine Bow peak station
evidence.quote: the cross bearing reported from Forest Guard Ramsay of the Medicine Bow peak station

evidence.supports: fire about three miles south of Mountain Home, on the Colorado forest
evidence.quote: about three miles south of Mountain Home and on the Colorado national forest

evidence.supports: county index lists Somber Hill as a gone tower (FFLOS US 2106, WY 8)
evidence.quote: Albany Somber Hill 41.07397 -106.18928 Tower Gone FFLOS US 2106, WY 8

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A July 1922 item calls Somber Hill a secondary lookout, with the primary station on Medicine Bow Peak. A 1930 Casper paper, quoted by the register, calls both primary lookouts. The story reports both.
Register says removed in the 1960s; firelookout.com says gone and gives no year. The story uses the register's decade.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height of 18.3 m matches the 60-foot steel tower reported in the 1927 item. The register's 'Removed 1960s' appears as 1960 in the events list; that year is approximate. The 1911 event refers to a wooden platform, not a tower. Staffing after 1932 is not documented in the sources read. The newspaper items come from westlookouts.weebly.com, which reprints them; the originals were not read. Access is unknown and no remains are described, so the story says so. No photo added.
